{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./avs-vtune.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -n 1        -> -n 1
#   -t 0:10:00  -> -t 10m
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 10m --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p qcpu_exp not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the qcpu_exp partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm -A DD-23-135 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require account/project out-of-band.

  # NOTE: Slurm --comment "use:vtune=2022.2.0" not translated.
  # Performance implication: if this comment triggers site-specific placement/software provisioning, omitting it could change performance/availability.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-type END not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notification.

  # NOTE: Slurm -J AVS-vtune not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm-specific $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR not available under Flux.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: using the wrong working directory could change I/O behavior.

  cd "${PWD}"

  ml intel-compilers/2022.1.0 CMake/3.23.1-GCCcore-11.3.0 VTune/2022.2.0-intel-2021b

  [ -d build_vtune ] && rm -rf build_vtune
  mkdir -p build_vtune
  cd build_vtune

  CC=icc CXX=icpc cmake ..
  make

  for threads in 18 36; do
      for builder in "ref" "loop" "tree"; do
          rm -rf vtune-${builder}-${threads}
          flux run -n 1 vtune -collect threading -r vtune-${builder}-${threads} -app-working-dir . -- \
            ./PMC --builder ${builder} -t ${threads} --grid 128 ../data/bun_zipper_res3.pts
      done
  done
fi
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
If there is a directive that does not translate, you MUST leave it out and add a comment about the performance implications of the omission.

1. Analyze the provided script below.
2. Write a new script and return in a json structure with a "jobspec"
